summary: StageLink auth audit — Iteration 1. Backend: 24/24 auth tests pass (register validation, login, brute-force lock @ 6 fails -> 429, refresh valid/invalid/wrong-type, /me valid/missing/malformed, logout, roles single+both, active-role gating). Frontend: 10/10 auth UI flows pass — root redirects unauth users to /auth/login, invalid login shows 'Invalid email or password', seeded musician login lands on Discover tabs, tokens saved in localStorage, session persists on reload, weak password shows client-side validation, strong password creates account -> /auth/role, choosing 'Both' assigns roles=[musician,organizer] -> /auth/onboarding, Sign out clears both tokens and returns to /auth/login. Auth layer looks production-ready. Two minor UX/testID improvements suggested (see action_items).

ui_bugs.issue: Sign-out button has no testID. Automation had to fall back to text matching. Add testID="logout-button".

issues: User picked 'Both' (roles=[musician,organizer], active_role=musician) but onboarding rendered organizer profile fields (Organization name) instead of musician fields matching active_role. Consider rendering onboarding based on active_role, or offering both profile forms sequentially. Not blocking auth audit — flagged for follow-up.

react_native_issues.issue: Console warning during tests: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents'. Non-blocking but should be cleaned up. Likely inside a third-party component or a manual pointerEvents prop.

action_items: (Minor) Add testID="logout-button" to the Sign-out Pressable in app/(tabs)/profile.tsx for reliable automation.

(Follow-up, out of auth-audit scope) When user picks 'Both' at role select, the /auth/onboarding screen currently shows organizer fields even though active_role='musician'. Decide product UX: run onboarding for active_role only, or force user to complete both profiles.
(Cleanup) Track down 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents' warning and migrate to style.pointerEvents.
critical_code_review_comments: Backend auth is well-structured: bcrypt hashing, JWT access(24h)+refresh(30d) with 'type' claim enforced (refresh cannot masquerade as access and vice-versa), lowercase email normalization, EmailStr validation, password policy (>=8, letters+numbers) enforced via Pydantic validator, brute-force lock at 6 fails / 10 min.

Brute-force protection is in-process memory dict (_login_attempts) — will reset on backend restart and not shared across multiple workers. Acceptable for single-worker dev; consider Redis/Mongo-backed rate limit for production scale.
JWT_SECRET falls back to hard-coded 'stagelink-dev-secret-change-me' if unset — safe for now (env has it) but consider fail-fast on missing secret in production builds.

/api/auth/logout is stateless — refresh tokens are NOT invalidated server-side after logout. A stolen refresh_token would remain valid until 30-day expiry. Consider a refresh-token blacklist (jti) collection for true logout invalidation.
Auth guard in _layout.tsx correctly handles four states (loading/unauthenticated/authenticated-no-roles/authenticated-not-onboarded/fully-authed). Look clean.
AuthContext token refresh flow uses a shared in-flight promise (refreshing.current) to prevent thundering-herd refresh — good pattern.
server.py is 846 lines — approaching the 700-line guideline threshold. Consider splitting auth / gigs / applications / AI into separate routers when adding more features.
